title: A validly signed card whose RSA signing key is 1024 bits
rationale: The violating case R8 leg 1 requires for C15, and the reason C15 was not demoted wholesale on 30 July 2026. Two of its three conditions lost their MUST when the primary text was read -- `none` and symmetric algorithms are governed by sentences binding the verifier, or by RFC 8725, which is about JWTs -- but this one survives intact: RFC 7518 3.3 puts a 2048-bit floor on the signer, in the document the check already cited, and it is mechanically observable from the published key set. Blanket-demoting C15 would have discarded a correctly anchored measurement to tidy up two badly anchored ones. The signature here genuinely verifies, which is the point of constructing it that way: the defect is the key length and nothing else, so the fixture isolates C15 from C04 instead of relying on a broken signature to produce the failure.
key_provenance: A real 1024-bit RSA key generated for this fixture; the private key was discarded after signing and appears nowhere. The protected header base64url-decodes to {"alg": "RS256", "kid": "agent-example-rsa-1024", "jku": "https://agent.example.org/.well-known/jwks.json"} and the signature is a genuine RS256 signature over `protected.JCS(card)`, so it would verify if the instrument attempted it. It does not attempt it: a 1024-bit RSA signature is not creditable as a cryptographic binding, and C04 therefore reports UNSPECIFIED rather than a verification failure that did not happen.

spec.quote: A key of size 2048 bits or larger MUST be used with these algorithms.
A signed card MUST be verifiable against a discoverable key.
